title: GitHub - morluto/rea: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries. · GitHub
claims: REA is an MCP-based reverse-engineering toolkit that connects AI agents to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron applications, .NET assemblies, and websites. Its documentation says analysis runs locally and returns evidence and limitations for conclusions.

REA does not itself automatically produce a finished software clone. Its official workflow is to inspect an application, return evidence, and let the connected coding agent implement a similar feature or behavior.

title: 6.9.0 advertised tool schemas contain \uD800 surrogate-class patterns that the DeepSeek official API rejects with 400 (worked in 6.8.0) · Issue #10436 · morluto/rea
claims: The claim that REA exposes 229 tools is accurate for the REA 6.8.0-era tool catalog. Official repository issue data records 229 advertised MCP tools, while later version 6.9.0 data records 255, so the number is version-dependent.

blocks.text: rea-agents 6.9.0 advertises \uD800 surrogate-class escape sequences in tool pattern fields. The DeepSeek official API rejects these schemas server-side with HTT
Register rea-agents@6.9.0 as an MCP server in any client that calls the DeepSeek official API.
Start a session. The very first model request fails; no tool call is needed.
Error returned by the DeepSeek API (request_id present, so this is server-side):
Invalid schema for function 'mcp__rea__binary_session': "^[^\uD800-\uDFFF]*$" is not a "regex" (code: INVALID_REQUEST, status: 400)
Version comparison (probed via MCP tools/list on the same host)
Tools whose advertised schema contains \uD800 escapes
binary_session → expected_server_path pattern list
binary_session advertised schema size
Affected tool names in 6.9.0 include: binary_session, close_binary, extract_artifact, inspect_plist, inspect_with_objdump, start_gdb_session, inspect_keyed_arch
The pattern ^[^\uD800-\uDFFF]*$ (no unpaired surrogates on path-like inputs) is valid ECMA-262 regex and legitimate JSON Schema, but several gateway validators
In 6.8.0 the compact input-schema profile stripped these annotations from advertised schemas. In 6.9.0 the compact profile passes canonical schemas through unch
The 6.9.0 release notes mention caring about "strict gateway translation" (compact enum/union normalization), so this looks like an untested corner of the same
Suggested fixes (any one suffices)
Rewrite the surrogate exclusion in a dialect-portable way in advertised schemas (e.g. strip the pattern from the advertised form; the server still validates can
Drop surrogate-class patterns from the compact/full advertised input schema for path-like strings, keeping them only in server-side validation.
Document REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE behavior change for 6.9.0 so clients pairing with strict gateways know to pin 6.8.0.

title: Someone Rebuilt Adobe in Rust with AI Agents. Is It Usable? | Flowtivity
claims: The Adobe story is based on ArtCraft, a project by developer Brandon Thomas. Reporting says seven Adobe-style applications were released under the ArtCraft brand between September 30 and October 1, 2026, including Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, Acrobat Pro, After Effects, and InDesign-style tools.

The claim that approximately eight Claude agents worked in parallel is supported by reporting on the ArtCraft workflow, which describes about eight Claude Opus 5.5 agents working on independent subsystems while a human handled integration and testing.

The Adobe apps were not complete replacements for Adobe Creative Cloud. The project’s reported self-assessment put professional daily-work parity at roughly 25% to 35%; 115 of 170 reference files reportedly rendered pixel-identically in one Photoshop-style test, or about 68%.
